Akpabio gave the assurance on Monday night while laying the foundation stone for the construction of Biology, Physics and Chemistry laboratories by the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI) at Independence High School, Essien Udim Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State.
He also pledged to mobilise the National Assembly to work with the presidency towards the effective implementation of the Federal Government’s empowerment policies, particularly those targeting vulnerable Nigerians.
“President Bola Tinubu is currently renewing the hope of our independence. There is a solemn covenant between a government and its people; a covenant greater than political parties, and more sacred than the privileges of public office.
“It is that power shall serve the people, authority shall advance their welfare, and leadership shall be judged not by the splendour of its promises, but by the substance of its achievements,” he said. The Senate President commended NASENI for implementing programmes aimed at improving the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians in line with the Renewed Hope Agenda of the Tinubu administration.
He also praised the agency’s Executive Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Khalil Suleiman Halilu, for what he described as its commitment to empowering struggling Nigerians through skills acquisition and technology-driven initiatives.
“I salute an institution that has chosen to honour that covenant. I commend the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure, NASENI, and its Executive Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Khalil Suleiman Halilu, for demonstrating that government can be a helping hand to the struggling, a ladder to the aspiring and a bridge between the poverty of today and the prosperity of tomorrow,” he said.
Akpabio said democracy should be measured by improvements in the living conditions of ordinary citizens, including farmers, artisans, unemployed youths and children from disadvantaged backgrounds.
He said, “Democracy is not vindicated by magnificent offices or eloquent declarations; it is vindicated when the farmer prospers, when the artisan earns an honest living, when the unemployed acquire productive skills and when the poorest child can look towards tomorrow with hope.”
Reflecting on the history of Independence High School, the Senate President said the institution represented the vision of Nigeria’s founding generation, who understood that political freedom must be complemented by education and knowledge.
He argued that Nigeria’s next phase of independence should focus on achieving scientific and technological self-reliance rather than depending on other countries for machinery, technology, scientific knowledge and economic opportunities.
“Our fathers fought to free our country from colonial rule. Our generation must fight to free its productive capacities from dependence. Our fathers raised the flag of political sovereignty. We must raise the standard of scientific and technological sovereignty,” he said.
Akpabio described the construction of the three science laboratories as an investment in future discoveries, inventions and industrial development, urging students, particularly girls, to pursue careers in science and technology.
He said the facilities could help nurture future scientists, engineers and innovators capable of developing solutions to critical national challenges.
Earlier, Halilu said the NASENI Sustainable Empowerment Programme and the construction of STEM laboratories in Ikot Ekpene Senatorial District were designed to address poverty by equipping residents with practical and technical skills.
He illustrated the importance of vocational training with the examples of a farmer unable to process harvested produce because of a faulty machine and a student who understands electrical circuits but has never had the opportunity to build one.
According to him, practical training would enable people to sustain businesses, improve their livelihoods and give young Nigerians the confidence and skills to develop solutions to local challenges. Halilu commended President Tinubu and Akpabio for supporting investments in technical education and practical skills development, saying such initiatives would create opportunities for Nigerians to earn a living within their communities.
The highlight of the event was the presentation of starter packs to 500 beneficiaries who completed hands-on training in 13 engineering trade areas, including solar installation, electronics repair, welding, refrigeration and compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicle conversion.
